title: Generate meeting notes fully in-browser with Chrome built-in AI, no server or cloud model
context: Recording transcripts needed AI meeting notes. The spec measured on the owner's Chrome 157 that LanguageModel is unavailable for Hebrew (en is downloadable), Summarizer is unavailable for Hebrew, and Translator he↔en is downloadable. Hebrew meetings therefore cannot be summarized directly by the built-in model.
decision: Notes are produced entirely in Chrome using built-in AI (Gemini Nano via Prompt API, Translator, LanguageDetector), with no Ollama, cloud calls, or extra installs. Hebrew transcripts go detect → translate to English → prompt in English → translate results back to the transcript language; English skips translation. Summaries, transcript edits, segments, and Q&A history are stored next to each recording in Documents\Meeting Recordings through new server routes.
consequences: Feature works only in Chrome with built-in AI; other browsers or unsupported devices see an explanation in the AI sections while the rest of the app works.
The first model download must be started from a user click (transient activation), so LanguageModel.create()/Translator.create() must run before any long await.
Hebrew summaries take extra translation passes, and translation results are cached in the summary file.

Server gains segments capture, a <id>.prev.txt backup before re-transcribe, transcript PUT, summary GET/PUT/DELETE, a route-specific 5 MB JSON limit, and delete now moves all <id>.* files to _deleted.
Summary goes stale when the transcript changes; sourceHash (SHA-256 of transcript text) drives a 'Regenerate' banner.
Speaker diarization is out of scope because no browser API provides it.
